dispositions.rationale: Sequential execution owns the authoritative source lock through postflight; parallel workers own clone-local locks and the coordinator acquires the distinct source lock only for final compare-and-swap publication.
Delegated-ineligible writers must represent their capability refusal through the closed common error registry.
This is implementation-documentation drift scheduled for the cross-surface contract task, not a contradiction in the reviewed specification prose.
The T-174 release matrix is intentionally a maintainer-owned release checklist and evidence map rather than a new binary-managed artifact schema.
The strict parallel result must carry the head and worker-evidence bindings that the feature contract requires it to validate.
Storage-neutral digest-bound review needs the selected spec raw-byte digest directly in the strict machine result.
Known producer workflows already carry exact review paths; a discovery command is a separately designed future reporting surface.
Persistent autonomous-run history conflicts with the explicit foreground result-file and no-run-database boundaries.
The specification explicitly excludes control over privileged or undetectable process escape and treats the caller-supplied process as trusted beyond detectable containment.
Portable verification history is intentionally lifecycle metadata; fresh attestation requires producer-local reports and is not claimed after those transient reports disappear.
Product-scope relevance is an external semantic prompt and review judgment; Taskrail mechanically enforces only declared lifecycle, planning, Git, and mutation invariants.
